abstract: Low-complexity causal speech separation must preserve speaker information and allocate residual mixture energy without relying on future feature frames. We present GTCRN-SS, a two-stage time-frequency separator that adapts the compact GTCRN enhancement backbone to fixed-output speech separation. The model combines internal residual allocation, reconstruction-conditioned refinement, and frame-aligned recurrent-state transfer. Its complex-mask estimator assigns non-target content to an unreturned residual branch, while the complementary speech estimate conditions a second stage whose final masks remain anchored to the original mixture. A lightweight low-rank adapter transfers causal recurrent evidence between recursive executions without adding another recurrent memory network. The neural graph excludes future feature frames and incurs only the fixed analysis look-ahead of the centered short-time Fourier transform. On noisy Libri2Mix, GTCRN-SS achieves 10.1 dB SDRi and 9.5 dB SI-SNRi with fewer than one million parameters and a low computational footprint. Independently trained ablations confirm the benefits of recurrent-state transfer and reconstruction conditioning, and corpus-level diagnostics show that the internal branch primarily captures residual rather than target-speech content. These results establish GTCRN-SS as an effective quality-efficiency operating point for causal monaural speech separation.

oneSentenceThesis: GTCRN-SS 把单输出增强主干改成两阶段因果分离，用内部残余分支守住混合谱能量守恒并给第二阶段提供语音和线索，在含噪 Libri2Mix 上以 0.9 M 参数取得 10.1 dB SDRi 和 9.5 dB SI-SNRi，但结论只在 8 kHz 双人含噪全 utterance 评测和固定短时傅里叶变换前瞻下成立。
originalTitle: GTCRN-SS: Lightweight Causal Speech Separation with Residual Allocation and Reconstruction Refinement
